brief: A gentle 40-second video for children aged five to eight about what lives in rock pools, and how to look without harming anything.

scenes.narration: When the tide goes out, it leaves little pools behind in the rocks.
scenes.visual: Low tide on a rocky shore, small pools shining in the morning sun, gentle waves far off, wide shot.

sentences.text: When the tide goes out, it leaves little pools behind in the rocks.

scenes.narration: Look closely. Each one is a tiny world.
scenes.visual: A slow push-in over a clear rock pool, seaweed swaying, light dancing on the bottom.

sentences.text: Each one is a tiny world.

scenes.narration: Sea anemones close up like flowers when you touch them, gently.
scenes.visual: Macro shot of a red sea anemone closing its tentacles, the water rippling.

sentences.text: Sea anemones close up like flowers when you touch them, gently.

scenes.narration: Crabs hide under the rocks, waiting for the water to come back.
scenes.visual: A small green shore crab scuttling under a rock ledge in shallow water, close to the ground.

sentences.text: Crabs hide under the rocks, waiting for the water to come back.

scenes.narration: Starfish hold on tight with hundreds of tiny tube feet.
scenes.visual: Close-up of an orange starfish on a rock, its tube feet moving slowly, crystal-clear water.

sentences.text: Starfish hold on tight with hundreds of tiny tube feet.

scenes.narration: Always put back any rock you lift, just the way you found it.
scenes.visual: A child’s hands carefully placing a flat rock back into a pool, the background soft.

sentences.text: Always put back any rock you lift, just the way you found it.

scenes.narration: Then let the tide come back and tuck them all in.
scenes.visual: The tide flowing back over the pools at sunset, waves gently covering the rocks, wide shot.

sentences.text: Then let the tide come back and tuck them all in.

title: Tide pools for kids
